[acl2024_fixture_001] Language systems must generalize beyond memorized examples. Prior evaluations often hide domain shifts.

We introduce fixture method 1 and state its scope. This synthetic text validates addressing only.

[acl2024_fixture_002] Reliable language processing requires explicit evaluation boundaries. Existing studies report mixed transfer results.

We present fixture method 2 under controlled assumptions. The record is not research evidence.

[acl2024_fixture_003] Scientific text contains claims with different evidential roles. Earlier benchmarks collapse these roles.

Our fixture method 3 separates the setup from its stated contribution. It exists for contract testing.

[acl2024_fixture_004] Model comparisons depend on stable inputs. Uncontrolled prompts weaken causal interpretation.

We describe fixture method 4 using deterministic records. No empirical conclusion follows from this sample.

[acl2024_fixture_005] Cross-domain writing presents both factual and rhetorical challenges. Many systems conflate these sources of variation.

Fixture method 5 isolates a small processing step. The wording is intentionally synthetic.

[acl2024_fixture_006] Reproducible experiments require stable document identifiers. Filename conventions alone are insufficient.

We assign fixture method 6 a deterministic identifier. Hashes protect the serialized contract.

[acl2024_fixture_007] Evidence spans should be recoverable from normalized text. Approximate offsets can obscure provenance failures.

Fixture method 7 records exact character boundaries. The check is entirely deterministic.

[acl2024_fixture_008] Paragraph structure provides a stable local address. Sentence segmentation must preserve source text.

We use fixture method 8 to test both coordinates. Whitespace normalization is versioned by implementation.

[acl2024_fixture_009] Condition comparisons require shared target evidence. Rebuilding inputs per condition can introduce drift.

Fixture method 9 produces one serialized pack. Every condition receives its recorded hash.

[acl2024_fixture_010] Gold text must remain outside generation inputs. Logical warnings are weaker than physical separation.

Fixture method 10 tests distinct output roots. Static audits protect compiler boundaries.

[acl2024_fixture_011] Token budgets influence the amount of conditioning information. Silent overages invalidate comparisons.

Fixture method 11 records counts before and after truncation. A shared controller applies the limit.

[acl2024_fixture_012] Compiler cost and writer cost answer different questions. Both must eventually be recorded.

Fixture method 12 defines only the adapter contract. No compiler is implemented in this stage.

[acl2024_fixture_013] Structured artifacts make experiment state inspectable. Noncanonical serialization can change hashes.

Fixture method 13 sorts object keys consistently. Unicode is preserved in UTF-8.

[acl2024_fixture_014] Pilot data should expose isolation defects cheaply. It should not be confused with final research data.

Fixture method 14 labels its synthetic status. The audit reports that label.

[acl2024_fixture_015] Source normalization must be repeatable across runs. Line ending differences should not alter logical paragraphs.

Fixture method 15 uses normalized newlines. Sentence text remains exactly addressable.

[acl2024_fixture_016] Target records contain visible, evidential, and withheld fields. A single broad loader risks accidental leakage.

Fixture method 16 writes separate namespace files. Downstream packages receive no gold loader.

[acl2024_fixture_017] Versioned configuration supports reproducible reruns. Defaults should be explicit rather than implicit.

Fixture method 17 records dataset and budget versions. Later stages can cite those values.

[acl2024_fixture_018] A pilot command should produce all required artifacts. Manual intermediate steps create avoidable variance.

Fixture method 18 uses one preparation entry point. Failure returns a nonzero status.

[acl2024_fixture_019] Automated audits should state the evidence they checked. A single boolean is insufficient for diagnosis.

Fixture method 19 retains per-check details. The report remains machine readable.

[acl2024_fixture_020] Stage gates prevent premature implementation. Passing ingestion does not authorize a compiler.

Fixture method 20 closes the Stage 1 boundary. Work stops before strategy extraction.
